amendments.rule: A verbless clause supplies its English copula from the construction, not from nothing. In *that it was good*, the supplied *it was* belongs to the unit headed on `טוֹב`; do not mark it `added`. **This covers the copula and nothing more.** Where the ASV instead supplies a whole *lexical* verb for a clause whose Hebrew has none — the allotment formula `וְלִבְנֵי קְהָת הַנּוֹתָרִים ... עָרִים עָשֶׂר` → *And unto the rest of the sons of Kohath* ***were given*** *by lot ... ten cities* — no morpheme's rendering that verb completes, and it is `added` under rule 30, together with any object the ASV supplies alongside it, as in *were given them*. Test by asking which morpheme is there to carry the English: `הָיָה` carries the *have* of rule 43 and the frame of rule 21, a Hebrew verb carries the light verb of rule 44, and a preposition that is itself the predicate carries the copula of rule 49 — but a preposition the ASV has already spent a word on, as in *unto the rest*, carries nothing further, and a clause with no verb in it at all licenses no verb. **The copula goes to the predicate, and an explicit subject takes only its own English.** Where the clause writes its subject — a pronoun such as `אָנֹכִי`, `אֲנִי`, `אַתְּ` or `הוּא`, or a subject noun — that morpheme takes the English pronoun or noun realizing it and nothing more, while the supplied *am*, *art*, *is*, *are* or *was* joins the predicate, exactly as rule 49 puts it on the preposition heading a prepositional predicate and rule 34 puts it on the predicate a gapped line licenses. `עֶבֶד אַבְרָהָם אָנֹכִי` → *I* ***am*** *Abraham's servant* gives *am* to `עֶבֶד` and *I* to `אָנֹכִי`; `בַּת מִי אַתְּ` → *Whose daughter* ***art*** *thou* gives *art* to `בַּת`; `הוּא אֲדֹנִי` → *It* ***is*** *my master* gives *is* to `אֲדֹנִי`; and `מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה` → *What man* ***is*** *this* gives *is* to `מִי`, which is the clause's predicate, leaving *this* to the demonstrative. Read the Hebrew clause for which side is the predicate rather than the English word order, since the copula stands beside the subject in every one of these; where the predicate's own words then stand apart from it, the unit is discontinuous under rule 25.
amendments.why: Rules 20, 34 and 49 all place the supplied copula with the predicate, but each states it for a clause with no competing candidate — a bare predicate, a gapped line, a prepositional phrase — and none says what happens when the clause writes an explicit subject pronoun beside which the English copula happens to stand. GEN.24 met that case five times and split three-to-two on it: 24.24 and 24.34 put the copula on the predicate noun, while 24.23, 24.47 and 24.65 put it on the pronoun, with nothing in the source licensing the difference. The corpus settles it in the same direction the majority of the contract already points: PSA.12.4 `אָדוֹן` → *is lord* and MAL.1.6 `אֲדוֹנִים` → *am a master*, the latter standing in a clause with its own explicit `אָנִי`, both give the copula to the predicate noun, and no unit in the searched corpus moves it onto a subject. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the gap is in rule 20's own sentence about where the copula belongs; a separate rule pointing back at it would leave the under-specified sentence in place for whoever reads it first.

conventions: Interrogative he: where the ASV asks by inversion and the fronted auxiliary is licensed by another morpheme, the he is unrepresented and the auxiliary stays with that morpheme - 'must' with 'ashiv at 24.5, 'Is' with the existential yesh at 24.23, 'Wilt' with telekhi at 24.58. Where the ASV writes an indirect-question 'whether', the he takes it (24.21). The corpus reads 1KI.21.20 the other way, giving 'hast' to the he, so this is the chapter's judgment and not a settled reading.

halakh plus 'acharei is rendered by the single English verb 'follow' (24.5, 24.8, 24.39, 24.61): the verb of going takes 'follow' and 'acharei is unrepresented under rule 40, since the ASV spends no word on what the preposition contributes. The suffix on 'acharei still takes its own pronoun.

The directive he is never unrepresented in this chapter. It takes the written English direction word where the ASV writes one (24.16, 24.32, 24.45, 24.52, 24.67), and joins the fused unit where one English word carries both the place and the direction - shammah -> 'thither' (24.6, 24.8), hachutsah -> 'out' (24.29).

ka'asher fused into a single 'as' or 'when' takes its head on the preposition rather than the relative (24.22, 24.51, 24.52). Both are defensible; the chapter chose the preposition and held to it in all three.

report: Read all 113 candidate groups and the verse dump end to end, including the added units the lemma table cannot see. Three real splits; six verses patched.

Split 1 - verbless nominal clause with an explicit subject pronoun. GEN.24.24 and 24.34 give the supplied copula to the predicate noun and leave the pronoun only its own English; GEN.24.23, 24.47 and 24.65 give it to the pronoun. Nothing in the source licenses the difference. Rules 20, 34 and 49 place the copula with the predicate, and the corpus agrees directly (PSA.12.4 adon -> 'is lord'; MAL.1.6 adonim -> 'am a master' beside its own ani -> 'I'). Patched 24.23, 24.47, 24.65; 24.24 and 24.34 already read that way and are untouched.

Split 2 - the interrogative he. GEN.24.5 and 24.23 leave it unrepresented and let the ASV's fronted auxiliary go to the morpheme that licenses it ('must' to ashiv, 'Is' to yesh); GEN.24.58 gives 'Wilt' to the he instead. Reconciling the other way is barred: it would take 'Is' off yesh and leave the existential holding only 'there', against rule 50's reasoning. Patched 24.58 to rule 17. Corpus 1KI.21.20 he -> 'hast' [medium] reads the other way; one hedged unit, so this is recorded as a convention and not promoted.

Split 3 - the directive he. GEN.24.29 folds it into the one-word fusion hachutsah -> 'out'; GEN.24.6 and 24.8 mark it unrepresented beside sham -> 'thither', on a note ('thither already carries the direction') that states the fusion premise and then declines it. 'Thither' carries both the place and the direction, so rule 30's wherein case applies. Patched 24.6 and 24.8; the chapter now never leaves a directive he unrepresented.

Cleared as non-splits: the presentative frames divide exactly as rule 45 requires (apodosis waw present in 24.15, 24.22, 24.30, 24.52; absent in 24.14 and 24.43, where the verb carries the 'that'); halakh acharei -> 'follow' is uniform across 24.5, 24.8, 24.39, 24.61; the added object pronouns of 24.41, 24.51 and 24.53 are correctly separated from the idiomatic 'bowed his head', 'went his way' and 'tarried all night', which fuse because they are what the verb's lexeme is rendered by (rule 44); the rule 29 article counting is consistent across all sixteen construct chains; and H853 is distinguished from H854 throughout, with 24.57 'inquire at' the one rule 16 first-family case.

BSB: no genuine error. The four recurring classes (Sp3ms resumptives, prepositions the recasting silences, articles with no written 'the', and waws the ASV drops) are the documented convention difference, and every individually named token resolves under a cited rule. Note that patching 24.58 removes an agreement, since BSB represents that he; rules 7 and 38 make that irrelevant, and the aggregate was not a consideration.

Left standing but worth a later reader's eye: GEN.24.11 gives the second le of le'et tset hash-sho'avot the relative 'that' under rule 52, though le governs 'et rather than the infinitive. It is defensible and single-verse, so it is not patched here.
